contributions.headingText: Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder (iNK-LPD) of the GI tract is an indolent but recurring EBV-negative NK-cell proliferation that predominantly involves the GI tract but may occasionally affect other anatomical sites.
97021/1 Indolent NK-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of gastrointestinal tract
2B3Z & XH5LU6 & XA9607 Neoplasms of haematopoietic or lymphoid tissues, unspecified & T/NK-cell lymphoma of gastrointestinal tract
Acceptable: atypical NK-cell proliferation of the gastrointestinal tract; lymphomatoid gastropathy; NK-cell enteropathy.

iNK-LPD involves the stomach (in ~70% of cases) and the small/large intestine (in ~30%) {16625103;20966166;31383643;20829373}. Similar lesions have been reported in the gallbladder {30212873;39276532;36494712}, and rarely in the vagina {31609783}, bladder {39276532}, nasopharynx {36494712}, and adjacent lymph nodes {32696224}.

Patients are asymptomatic or have vague gastrointestinal symptoms including abdominal pain, with lesions identified on endoscopy. Lower limb oedema, possibly secondary to hypoalbuminaemia, has also been reported uncommonly {39276532}. There is no history of coeliac disease or inflammatory bowel disease, and no systemic lymphadenopathy or organomegaly {20966166;31383643;20829373}.
iNK-LPD is rare. Patients are usually men and women in their third to eighth decades of life {20966166;31383643;20829373}.

The proliferation in iNK-LPD may be an immune response to antigen(s) encountered in the gastrointestinal mucosa {20966166;20829373}. A high prevalence of Helicobacter pylori infection has been reported in the gastric cases {20829373}, and an anecdotal report of regression of chronic recurrent disease after anti-Helicobacter therapy {35474034} suggests a possible etiological role of Helicobacter.

The most frequent mutation involves JAK3, which is present in 30% of cases tested {31383643;39276532;36494712}. Other mutated genes reported include, RUNX1T1, CIC, ERBB4, SETD5 {31383643}, BRAF, KRAS, FOXO3, CREBBP, and RP1L1 {36494712;39276532}. Strong immunostaining for phosphorylated STAT5 in all studied cases suggests that JAK-3/STAT5 pathway hyperactivation plays a role in pathogenesis {31383643;36494712}. These findings further suggest that iNK-LPD is neoplastic.

Endoscopy reveals single or multiple superficial small lesions, approximately 10–20 mm, manifesting as elevated lesions, often with hyperaemia (blood blister–like lesion), erosion, or ulcer, involving single or multiple sites along the GI tract {20966166;20829373}.

The lamina propria in iNK-LPD shows expansion by a relatively well-circumscribed but confluent infiltrate of medium-sized to large cells with irregular nuclei (occasionally with distinct nucleoli), finely clumped chromatin, and a moderate amount of pale cytoplasm {20966166;31383643;20829373}, often with paranuclear eosinophilic cytoplasmic granules {20829373}. Glands are displaced or destroyed. Epithelial invasion can be seen especially in gastric cases {20829373}. Necrosis is occasionally seen, usually with mucosal ulceration. Other inflammatory cells (plasma cells, neutrophils, eosinophils) are often present. The muscularis mucosae remains intact. There is no angiocentric-angiodestructive growth, villous atrophy, or crypt hyperplasia.

Immunohistochemistry and in situ hybridization

Lesional cells express CD2, CD56, CD7, cCD3, TIA1, and granzyme B, but they do not express sCD3, TCRαβ, TCRγδ, CD5, CD4, CD10, CD20, PAX5, CD138, or CD68. CD8 is rarely positive {25929350}. The Ki-67 proliferation index is usually low but can be as high as 80% {39276532}. In situ hybridization for EBV-encoded small RNA (EBER) is negative.

Differential diagnosis

There is significant immunophenotypic overlap between iNK-LPD and extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma, so their distinction is important to avoid unnecessary therapy. NK-large granular lymphocytic leukaemia differs from iNK-LPD by showing systemic (peripheral blood and marrow) involvement. See #49464Table 12.03 for differential diagnostic features.
In situ hybridization for EBER is negative. No clonal TR gene rearrangements have been identified {20966166;31383643;20829373}.

Essential: an infiltrate of atypical medium-sized to large lymphoid cells with pale cytoplasm and an NK-cell immunophenotype, confined to the superficial mucosa of the GI tract and rarely presenting at other anatomical sites, including lymph nodes; EBV negative.

Desirable: absence of clonal TR gene rearrangements.

Individual lesions usually regress spontaneously in a few months, but some patients may have persistent lesions or recurrent new lesions. Patients with iNK-LPD usually do not show a prolonged response to chemotherapy {20966166;31383643;20829373}. Progression to more aggressive disease has not been reported.
